{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUH0sFs8AAAABUaNm6w", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlSCSzg973n8", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlSCS", "number": 33, "title": "Add concise Issue/PR templates and development/review guidelines", "body": "## Problem

Refloom has mechanical verification and review requirements in `.fleet/project.yaml`, but it does not currently have repository-level Issue/PR templates or concise development/review guidance that defines what an appropriately scoped change looks like.

This is especially important for AI-assisted development. A change can be wrong in two opposite directions:

- **Incomplete:** it claims to resolve an Issue while leaving required work unresolved.
- **Over-scoped:** it adds abstractions, refactors, extensibility, policies, compatibility layers, or other complexity that the Issue does not justify.

The repository should make the expected development flow and review standard explicit without creating a large process framework.

## Expected outcome

Add a small set of repository guidance/templates, using GitWeave as the primary reference:

- GitWeave development flow: https://github.com/takahirox/gitweave/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md
- GitWeave review guidelines: https://github.com/takahirox/gitweave/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md
- GitWeave Issue template: https://github.com/takahirox/gitweave/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md
- GitWeave PR template: https://github.com/takahirox/gitweave/blob/main/.github/pull_request_template.md

The intended principle is essentially:

> **Complete, but no more.** Prefer the smallest change that fully satisfies the Issue.

Review should explicitly check both directions:

1. **No missing scope** — a PR must not claim to close an Issue unless it fully addresses the Issue.
2. **No unnecessary scope** — a PR should not introduce changes or complexity that are not justified by the Issue.

If a PR intentionally addresses only part of an Issue, it should say so clearly and should not present the Issue as resolved.

## Suggested minimal contents

The exact filenames and wording should be chosen during implementation, but the GitWeave structure is a good default and should be preferred unless Refloom has a concrete reason to differ.

### Issue template

Keep it small, similar to GitWeave:

- Problem
- Expected outcome
- Context

The Issue defines the scope. If requirements are unclear, clarify the Issue instead of inventing requirements during implementation.

### Pull Request template

Keep it small, similar to GitWeave:

- Summary
- Outcome
- Validation
- Related Issue(s)

A short scope check may be useful if it materially improves review discipline, for example:

- Does this PR fully address what it claims to resolve?
- Does it avoid unrelated or speculative work?

Do not turn the PR template into a long checklist unless there is demonstrated value.

### Development flow

Document the default flow:

```text
Issue
  ↓
Implementation
  ↓
Pull Request
  ↓
Review
  ↓
Revision if needed
  ↓
Merge
```

A PR should only claim to close an Issue when it fully addresses it.

### Review guidelines

Review should start from the source Issue and ask:

> Is this PR a complete and appropriately scoped solution to the Issue?

Check for both missing work and unnecessary work. In particular, watch for unnecessary abstractions, speculative extensibility, unrelated refactoring, new frameworks/subsystems, compatibility machinery, configuration, or policy that has no demonstrated need.

Additional complexity is not automatically beneficial. Prefer the smallest design that completely solves the stated problem.

Ordinary correctness still matters: expected behavior, architectural coherence, appropriate validation, and documentation updates when documented behavior changes.

## Repository language

Repository collaboration artifacts should be written in **English**, including at least:

- Issues
- Pull Requests
- review comments and other repository discussion/comments
- documentation
- code comments intended to remain in the repository

This keeps the repository and its development history consistently accessible to contributors and AI development/review agents.

Do not impose English on user-facing product content merely because repository collaboration uses English.

## Keep this change itself small

GitWeave already expresses most of the desired policy well. Prefer adapting/reusing that structure rather than inventing a substantially larger governance system.

This Issue does **not** require:

- a large CONTRIBUTING framework if the smaller GitWeave-style documents are sufficient,
- new CI or bots solely to enforce prose policy,
- additional approval layers,
- a broad coding-style guide,
- speculative contribution processes for future team structures,
- unrelated changes to Fleet configuration.

Add only Refloom-specific differences that are actually needed, such as the English-language repository rule above.

## Acceptance intent

After this change, a contributor or AI agent should be able to determine, without guessing:

- how work should move from Issue to PR to review to merge,
- that an Issue defines the intended scope,
- that a PR claiming completion must fully satisfy that Issue,
- that partial work must be identified as partial,
- that over-engineering and unjustified scope are review failures,
- that review checks both completeness and restraint,
- that validation remains required,
- and that repository collaboration/documentation is written in English.

The implementation should remain concise and should itself follow the same **complete, but no more** principle.", "url": "https://github.com/takahirox/refloom/issues/33", "created_at": "2026-10-01T15:22:30Z", "state": "OPEN", "repository": "takahirox/refloom", "labels": ["task"], "priority": null, "status": "In Progress", "is_archived": false}, "context": {}, "resources": {}, "allocation": {}, "instruction": null, "run_id": "c9459b08cf26415f919600f55d625511"}
